risks: Contractor footage: GFOE pilots / OET partners. rights-scout must confirm each clip is NOAA's own work (CLAUDE.md lesson: contractor/co-produced reels get overturned).
Broken duration metadata on two Commons webms: prefer NOAA's own mp4 masters; ffprobe before analysis.
Audio tracks (ROV chatter/narration) must be stripped; own narration + music only.
Slow footage = retention risk: needs speed-ups, punch-in zooms, tight 4-6 s windows; payoff energy low.
Planet Extremes adjacency (extreme environments): keep the comedy/behaviour angle, no depth/pressure fact rankings.
Anthropomorphism is a joke, not a claim; species names must match NOAA captions; no invented facts.
Demand unproven: no view data for this format; treat pilot as the measurement.

disagreements: Scout A picked silent stunts (A ranked feasibility 85); B scored them 74 and flagged IA provenance; spot-check sides with B (400x300 'HD', restoration-release Keaton copies, unknown IA transfer).

B and C both found the NOAA pool but framed it differently (B 'weirdos' = generic wonder, C 'unimpressed' = a joke criterion). C's criterion wins: it is the brand's comedic voice and NOAA's own captions support it.
A and C both proposed astronauts; A marked portfolio 45, C 58. Judge sides lower (30): same NASA ISS pool and look as Mission Voices.
A treats trend ideas as the demand signal; all three scouts agree trend and clearable footage are anti-correlated here, so trend ideas fail the gate.
